messages.subject: Flying Monkeys!
parts:
Hi all,

Our sponsor, Revolution Analytics, sent along a box of goodies today, including a bunch of these amazing Super R Flying Monkeys:



From now on all anyone who gives a talk at D-RUG gets a T-shirt or a monkey.  Speaking of which, we need speakers for slots after this week.  Sign up and get your monkey!  This week, Mason Earles is earning with a brief talk on how he interfaces R with the Forest Vegetation Simulator, which is written in a different language.

I'll also give these away as prizes to whomever answers the most R questions on the listserv this academic year. I'm pretty sure Vince Buffalo and David J. Harris are in the lead.

 - Noam

messages.author: dbff4022aedcff7d
messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: Flying Monkeys!
parts:
Here's a question for you all in the spirit of flying monkeys,

Does anyone have experience using lmPerm? Have you used it on a mixed model? 

I am using it for a selection analysis to conduct permutation anovas and regressions.  The documentation says that it handles random effects, but does not specify much more. I would like to ultimately generate a permute a model that I created in lme.  From a bit of trial and error it seems that it is doing something with the random effect, I would just feel more comfortable if I knew exactly what that is. I can give some examples if that would be helpful.

On another note, I would be happy to run through my demographic analyses at some time if folks are still interested.

Kara
